assets.name: m_26_14-ai-audit
assets.description: M-26-14 D-06: the AI audit store. One document per Agent Builder trace span, copied by the m_26_14-ai-audit latest transform from traces-agent_builder.otel-* and normalized toward ECS by m_26_14-ai-audit-normalize (LRA 5.5 AI-system logging). attributes stays flattened on purpose - the gen_ai semantic conventions are experimental and field churn must not create mapping conflicts. Lifecycle: m_26_14-derived-store (hot only, no rollover, no delete) because this is a fixed-name latest-transform destination rewritten in place - the m_26_14-logs-hva-extended policy it carried before 0.3.1 rolls over in its hot phase, which on a plain index without a write alias parks ILM in ERROR (review finding R-48). HVA retention per LRA 8.1 is enforced on the SOURCE trace stream, which the genai stage binds to m_26_14-logs-hva-extended; the store itself never deletes. Integrity hashing happens HERE (final_pipeline) because Elasticsearch rejects index.final_pipeline in data stream settings, so the managed trace stream itself cannot hash; the stream gets the HVA ILM binding only (data stream settings API, genai stage).

assets.name: m_26_14-alert-coverage-metrics
assets.description: Index template for M-26-14 alert coverage metrics produced by the daily and latest transforms. Fixed-name transform destinations, so the lifecycle is m_26_14-derived-store (no rollover, no delete; review finding R-48)

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-baselines
assets.description: Asset configuration baseline snapshots for drift detection. Each document is a point-in-time baseline of a canonical asset (from m_26_14-assets): identity, OS version, and a configuration hash. The Asset Drift dashboard compares current state against these snapshots; the m_26_14-asset-drift pipeline (called from m_26_14-asset-canonical-enrich on every entity-resolution checkpoint) writes m_26_14.drift_detected onto the canonical record when current state diverges from the latest baseline.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-canonical
assets.description: Layer 3 canonical asset index — one document per resolved device, upserted by asset.id

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-inventory-normalized
assets.description: Layer 2 normalized asset events — all sources mapped to unified asset.* schema

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-triage
assets.description: Disposition ledger for unknown-device triage. One doc per asset.id (idempotent _id), written by _reindex from m_26_14-assets through the m_26_14-asset-triage-classify pipeline. Holds the computed m_26_14.triage.* disposition + evidence and the case-routing state (proposed -> routed -> actioned -> closed). The m_26_14-unknown-device-triage workflow reads this ledger to open disposition-specific Kibana Cases and records routing state here. The canonical store m_26_14-assets is NEVER mutated by triage — keeping the classification out of the continuous entity-resolution transform's latest-wins path (see project_demo_data_sources clobber note). host.name and disposition are keyword for aggregation/enrich.

assets.name: m_26_14-authorized-software-catalog
assets.description: Authorized software catalog (SWAM allowlist) — enrich source index for the m_26_14-authorized-software enrich policy used by the m_26_14-osquery-normalize pipeline. One doc per package name; carries authorization state, category, publisher, EOL flag, and CDM approval provenance (approved_by / approval_ref / min_version).

assets.name: m_26_14-config
assets.description: Single-document configuration index: the only place a threshold lives. Holds the LRA publication date (drives deadline countdowns), Appendix C per-element/per-level thresholds (editable when CISA's LRA publishes), retention day targets, scoring cadence, and operator attestations for properties Elasticsearch cannot observe (encryption at rest on ECE/self-managed, GRC two-gate retirement). Seed document ships in M3. @timestamp (seeded) and the raw_retention block are mapped so ES|QL posture rules can window and read them (the detection engine filters every ES|QL source on @timestamp): rule m_26_14-hva-retention-lock-drift alerts when raw_retention.hva is no longer keep_locked (D-12/D-18). thresholds.skew_seconds (document skew flag, m_26_14-timestamp-skew) and thresholds.ntp_offset_ms (host attestation, evidence.ntp_attestation; mirrored in the m_26_14-ntp-offset-exceeded rule) added for D-20. The unit-costs row (D-19: hot/frozen/blended USD per GB-month, all 0.0 as shipped) is mapped as doubles; the m_26_14-ops-metrics-snapshot workflow copies it onto each daily snapshot and m_26_14-ops-metrics-derive prices from it.

assets.name: m_26_14-data-classification-requests
assets.description: Audit log for data-classification intake requests written by the m_26_14-data-classification-intake workflow and queried by the m_26_14-classification-audit-query agent tool. Append-only: current state = most recent doc per index_name.

assets.name: m_26_14-ea-telemetry
assets.description: Seeded demonstration and validation telemetry stream logs-m_26_14_ea.telemetry-* (host, identity, process, file and network events shaped like the Windows, Linux, Entra ID and Okta integrations that the pack's rules, ML jobs and Entity Store engines read). Written by the planning repository's tools/seed_ea_telemetry.py; on an agency estate the equivalent events arrive on the integrations' own streams. Lives in the pack (review finding R-80, 2026-09-18) so the D-04 stream-hygiene lint covers it and every m_26_14.* field the m_26_14-final chain writes is mapped before the first document; the first pubsec install dynamic-mapped m_26_14.policy.sharing_class and provenance.transformations as text because the template was seeder-owned. Binds m_26_14-retention-l1 like the generic family; the seeder can point one stream at another pack policy through the data stream's own settings for a retirement walk.

assets.name: m_26_14-field-fidelity
assets.description: M-26-14 A-3 (D-02/16): hourly per-dataset field-fidelity scores against the LRA 6.3 common-field and App D category contracts.

assets.name: m_26_14-hash-coverage
assets.description: Dest index for the m_26_14-hash-coverage-rollup transform. Pre-created mapping: transform delivers group_by keys as flat dotted fields; @timestamp (max agg) is required so ML datafeeds and ES|QL rules can time-filter dest docs.

assets.name: m_26_14-host-alert-summary
assets.description: Destination index for the m_26_14-host-alert-summary transform — the COMPUTED rogue signal (Security alerts pivoted per host.name). Pre-created at bootstrap so the m_26_14-host-alert-lookup enrich policy can be PUT before the transform's first checkpoint (PUT _enrich/policy validates its source index exists). host.name MUST be keyword for the enrich match_field; the remaining pivot fields (alert_count, max_risk_score, last_alert, severities, rule_names) map dynamically.

assets.name: m_26_14-ingest-latency
assets.description: Dest index for the m_26_14-ingest-latency transform (D-03, LRA 3.5 timeliness): hourly lag percentiles per dataset with category thresholds and breach flags.

assets.name: m_26_14-jit-audit-reports
assets.description: Daily JIT access audit reports written by the m_26_14-jit-audit watcher: counts plus grant detail arrays for active and stale (expired-but-unrevoked) JIT grants. Grant arrays are flattened; drill into m_26_14-jit-grants for full grant records.

assets.name: m_26_14-jit-grants
assets.description: JIT (just-in-time) access grant register for Element 5 Level 4. Each grant is one document; the grant itself is implemented as an Elasticsearch role mapping named m_26_14-jit-{grant_id} so revocation is a single idempotent DELETE _security/role_mapping call. The m_26_14-jit-expiry watcher revokes expired grants every 15 minutes; the m_26_14-jit-audit watcher reports daily on grants active >72h.

assets.name: m_26_14-logs-data-streams
assets.description: Index template for logs-m_26_14.* data streams (the dot-form telemetry family: dns, auth, network, endpoint, ws, default and any agency dataset routed here). Applies ECS mappings and, through the m_26_14-log-integrity-settings component, the m_26_14-final chain. Binds m_26_14-retention-l1 (365 days, hot then frozen; the Initial-level floor of the LRA's retention framing) as the honest default lifecycle; raise a stream to a higher tier by overriding index.lifecycle.name on its own template or on the stream's settings (review finding R-79, 2026-09-18: before this the family inherited the stock logs policy).

assets.name: m_26_14-logs-hva-data-streams
assets.description: Index template for logs-m_26_14.*-hva* data streams (decision D-18, LRA 5.5 / App D.9). Same mapping family and integrity hashing as m_26_14-logs-data-streams, plus the m_26_14-logs-hva-extended ILM policy: HVA-routed streams keep a longer searchable window automatically. Wins over the general template on the -hva namespace by priority. Priority 299 sits above the general family (200) and below the dataset-specific templates (300+), so streams with their own template (software_inventory, osquery, netobserved, asset inventory) keep their mappings and ILM even on a -hva namespace; the HVA window uplift targets the general log-telemetry family.

assets.name: m_26_14-network-observed-devices
assets.description: Passively-observed network device inventory data stream (OT/IoT network visibility). Fed by NetFlow/IPFIX, DHCP, DNS, ARP, Packetbeat, Suricata observations via the m_26_14-network-device-normalize pipeline. Every source.mac/ip on the wire becomes an unmanaged asset + Entity Store host entity — the passive complement to osquery HWAM (agent-based). M-26-14 Appendix A HWAM / network visibility.

assets.name: m_26_14-ntp-status
assets.description: Latest NTP sample per host, written by the m_26_14-ntp-status latest transform from metrics-system.ntp-*. host.name MUST be keyword for the m_26_14-ntp-enrich policy to match. system.ntp.offset is nanoseconds (System integration field definition); consumers convert to milliseconds. Fixed-name transform destination: lifecycle m_26_14-derived-store (no rollover, no delete).

assets.name: m_26_14-observed
assets.description: Ledger index for entity observation state. Written by the m_26_14-observed-assets transform; one doc per entity (real hostname or observed-<ip>@<collector> for IP-keyed devices). host.name MUST be keyword (not text) for the m_26_14-observed-enrich policy to match correctly. If this index already exists with dynamic text mapping, DELETE it and _stop/_reset/_start the observed-assets transform to rebuild with this template. Consult the transform _meta sync_caveat before resetting. The first_log field (min @timestamp, added to the transform in M8) drives per-entity empirical retention horizons in the scoring engine.

assets.name: m_26_14-ops-metrics
assets.description: Index template for the daily D-19 ops-metrics snapshots written by the m_26_14-ops-metrics-snapshot workflow into monthly indices m_26_14-ops-metrics-YYYY-MM (store size, doc counts, frozen-tier split, agency unit costs). default_pipeline m_26_14-ops-metrics-derive computes the hot/frozen split, bytes per document and the estimated monthly cost from the rates in force (review finding R-45). Monthly plain indices, not one fixed index, so the m_26_14-metrics-store ILM policy (no rollover) can age them out (review finding R-48).

assets.name: m_26_14-osquery-hardware-inventory
assets.description: Hardware inventory data stream for M-26-14 Element 1 (HWAM)

assets.name: m_26_14-osquery-network-inventory
assets.description: Network interface inventory data stream for M-26-14 network visibility

assets.name: m_26_14-osquery-software-inventory
assets.description: Software inventory data stream for M-26-14 Element 2 (SWAM)

assets.name: m_26_14-osquery-user-inventory
assets.description: osquery local-user snapshot stream (feeds the m_26_14-asset-new-local-user rule). Producer: osquery users table snapshots emitting host.name + user.name per local account.

assets.name: m_26_14-oui-catalog
assets.description: MAC OUI (Organizationally Unique Identifier) → vendor + device_class catalog. Enrich source index for the m_26_14-oui-vendor enrich policy used by the m_26_14-network-device-normalize pipeline. One doc per 24-bit OUI prefix (lowercase colon form, e.g. 00:1d:9c). ot=true flags industrial/ICS/BMS vendors. Starter set — replace/extend with your agency's OT/IoT vendor inventory or a full IEEE OUI export.

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-policy
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07: per-dataset PEP policy rows (type policy: minimize list, sensitivity, sharing class, restricted routing) and the managed-exceptions register (type exception: rule, reason, approver, expiry). Enrich policy m_26_14-pep-policy-lookup serves the rows to the PEP pipelines; re-execute it after editing rows.

assets.name: m_26_14-pipeline-health
assets.description: M-26-14 D-04: mapping-conflict findings and run summaries written by the m_26_14-mapping-conflict-check workflow (LRA 4.7/7.3, App E.5.3). Plain index, not a data stream: low volume, one summary doc per day plus conflicts.

assets.name: m_26_14-production-ledger
assets.description: M-26-14 D-11: the production ledger. One manifest per authorized external production (LRA Section 7.4, App C.9.5/E.9.4): who asked, what was in scope, every transformation and redaction applied, source and output counts and hashes, the snapshot preserving the produced set, and the operator. Written by the m_26_14-authorized-production workflow; the runbook covers manual productions.

assets.name: m_26_14-retention
assets.description: Empirical dataset-retention holding index (decision #22). Written by m_26_14-dataset-retention transform; one doc per data_stream.dataset value. Serves two purposes: (1) enrich source for m_26_14-observed-enrich-based retention lookups in Stage 1; (2) source for the m_26_14-score-dataset-retention transform which projects per-dataset retention score docs into m_26_14-scores. Key field: horizon_days = (ingest_time - min(@timestamp)) / 86400000 -- the empirical searchable horizon. Replaces ILM/tier/snapshot introspection (old fetch_retention in score.py). The snapshot/'retrievable' axis is dropped; a single empirical axis is used and fed to both s_days and r_days in retention_level(). After re-running the transform or fresh data, re-execute the m_26_14-retention-enrich policy to refresh the snapshot.

assets.name: m_26_14-retirement-requests
assets.description: Audit log and state machine for the two-gate data retirement chain (Element 4, memo Appendix C Log Management at Optimal). Append-only since review finding R-71: every state transition is a new document with a time-suffixed id (the watchers and workflows used deterministic ids that overwrote the pending record). Current state = most recent record per index_name by @timestamp; hand-written records (approve, cancel, release from a Case) are stamped with @timestamp, updated_at and event.ingested by the default pipeline m_26_14-retirement-ledger (R-70). The loader pre-creates the index so the DM rules, the retention-readiness panels and the retirement-audit tool do not error on an absent index (R-73).

assets.name: m_26_14-scores
assets.description: Scoring output: one document per (asset x element x run), written by the m_26_14 transforms (M3). element is one of: inventory | coverage | operations | retention | log_mgmt | waterline. score is the Appendix C level achieved: 0=Ineffective, 1=Basic, 2=Intermediate, 3=Advanced, 4=Optimal (naming per Elastic public messaging on the M-26-14 five-level model). evidence holds the raw numbers behind the score; read it to understand any score. Dashboards are pure presentation over this index.

assets.name: m_26_14-software-inventory
assets.description: Common (source-agnostic) software inventory stream for M-26-14 Element 2 (SWAM). Software records from ANY collector converge here via reroute: osquery (m_26_14-osquery-normalize), customer CMDB/EDR (m_26_14-asset-normalize), etc. Default pipeline m_26_14-software-enrich applies the authorized-software catalog. SWAM dashboards query this pattern. Renamed from logs-m_26_14.software_inventory into the logs-m_26_14_asset.* family (review finding R-80, 2026-09-18) so every pack-owned inventory stream is underscore-form and the dot-form logs-m_26_14.* family is left to agency telemetry.

assets.name: m_26_14-software-latest
assets.description: Dest index for the m_26_14-software-latest transform (feeds the m_26_14-asset-security-software-removed rule). Pre-created mapping: transform delivers group_by keys as flat dotted fields.

assets.name: m_26_14-store-feed
assets.description: Entity Store v2 discovery feed (decisions #18/#21). Written by the m_26_14-store-feed transform; add this index pattern to the Security default data view so the store mints entities for devices it cannot discover from raw documents (syslog-named, observers, hostname-less). Maps host.name as keyword (NOT dynamic text). Dest pipeline promotes data_stream.dataset and event.module attestation onto feed docs so entity.source on discovered hosts shows which log streams referenced them. Discovered entities carry no asset.id. Do NOT add the full m_26_14-observed ledger to the data view.

assets.name: m_26_14-validation-ledger
assets.description: M-26-14 D-09/D-10/D-15: the validation ledger. Canary verdicts (kind: canary; three stages arrived/parsed/alerted per source class), retrieval-drill evidence (kind: retrieval_drill; query latencies with tier attribution, restore verification, hash check), and monthly ATT&CK coverage snapshots (kind: attack_coverage; enabled-rule counts and disabled-rule names against the pack's static technique table in docs/attack-coverage.md). Validation itself becomes citable evidence (LRA 3.5 Validation measure, App E.7.2/E.12, Sections 3.1/9.1).

assets.name: m_26_14-log-integrity-settings
assets.description: Component template: the one binding point for the pack final chain. Applies m_26_14-final as final_pipeline (D-03 ingest-lag measurement + D-04 schema observables + D-18 asset context + D-17 zero-trust context + D-07 policy enforcement, chaining m_26_14-log-integrity-hash SHA-256 integrity hashing) AND maps the fields the chain writes that composing templates do not map themselves: event.original (hashed, never indexed), m_26_14.zt.* (D-17), m_26_14.ingest_error and tags (R-35 failure contract), m_26_14.policy.pep_failed (fail-closed marker), m_26_14.policy.exception_expired / exception_rules_* (DC-1 managed-exception verdict) and exception_applied (DC-16: the PEP stages an active exception switched off for this document), event.hash and event.integrity.* (the canonical integrity hash, DC-2) and m_26_14.integrity_hash (one-release copy of event.hash, DC-2), m_26_14.ingest_lag_ms / ingest_lag_negative (D-03), m_26_14.skew_* (B.3 timestamp accuracy), m_26_14.schema.* and m_26_14.provenance.transformations (D-04/D-13), m_26_14.policy.sensitivity / sharing_class / hva / redacted / route_to_restricted (D-07 verdict) and asset.criticality / asset.managed (D-18 feeder). Found on the first pubsec install (2026-09-18): a stream composing only this template dynamic-mapped m_26_14.policy.sharing_class as text and m_26_14.provenance.transformations as text, so neither could be aggregated. Composed by logs-m_26_14.*, logs-m_26_14.*-hva* and the seven inventory-family templates; an agency template that composes it gets the same binding and mappings (the ea telemetry seeder does exactly that). Rule: a field written by m_26_14-final or its sub-pipelines is mapped here or in every composing template, never left to dynamic mapping; the D-04 stream-hygiene lint resolves composed_of and enforces it.

assets.name: m_26_14-ai-audit-normalize
assets.description: M-26-14 D-06: normalizes Agent Builder trace spans into the m_26_14-ai-audit store shape. Span attributes arrive as FLAT dotted keys (attributes['gen_ai.conversation.id']), which nested-path copy_from cannot reach, so one Painless script surfaces the gen_ai.* fields (never overriding existing values; content fields exist only when the six agentBuilder tracing privacy settings allow). Applied as the dest pipeline of the m_26_14-ai-audit transform (stable name, bootstrap-installed); the store template's final_pipeline then adds the D-08 integrity hash, since data stream settings reject index.final_pipeline and the managed trace stream cannot hash at source.

assets.name: m_26_14-alert-category-pipeline
assets.description: M-26-14 Element 3: Extracts Appendix B category from kibana.alert.rule.tags and denormalizes to m_26_14.category for ML datafeed partitioning.

assets.name: m_26_14-alert-coverage-daily-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for the m_26_14-alert-coverage-daily transform (daily alert counts per Appendix B category). Design call DC-4 (2026-09-18): every transform output carries the D-13 provenance append and derived stamp (producer, method, pack version, computation time) so consumer-without-producer and unstamped-derived-data classes are closed for this store. No field logic here; the transform body owns the aggregation.

assets.name: m_26_14-alert-coverage-latest-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for the m_26_14-alert-coverage-latest transform (latest alert per rule). Design call DC-4 (2026-09-18): every transform output carries the D-13 provenance append and derived stamp (producer, method, pack version, computation time) so consumer-without-producer and unstamped-derived-data classes are closed for this store. No field logic here; the transform body owns the aggregation.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-baseline-hash
assets.description: Post-transform pipeline for the baseline snapshot index. Stamps the snapshot timestamp so each baseline record carries the time it was captured.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-canonical-enrich
assets.description: Runs on every document written to m_26_14-assets by the entity resolution Transform. Unwraps top_metrics wrapped values, normalizes null strings and boolean strings, stamps timestamp, evaluates Element 1/2 coverage criteria, computes baseline state hash for drift detection.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-context
assets.description: M-26-14 D-18 HVA feeder: asset.criticality and asset.managed from m_26_14-assets by host.name (enrich m_26_14-asset-liveness), additive. Called from m_26_14-final before the policy enforcement point.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-drift
assets.description: Computes m_26_14.drift_detected (mirrored to asset.compliance.drift_detected): true when the asset's current baseline_hash diverges from its certified baseline hash, looked up by asset.id from the frozen m_26_14-asset-baselines snapshot. Replaces the drift watcher of the earlier design, which was never built; recomputed on every transform checkpoint so it is stable across re-enrichment.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-entity-store-enrich
assets.description: Enriches incoming security alert and log events with M-26-14 asset compliance context. Looks up the source host.name in m_26_14-assets and attaches asset.type, asset.criticality, m_26_14.element1_covered, m_26_14.element2_covered, and compliance fields. Enables Security UI and Entity Store records to surface readiness posture alongside risk scores.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-normalize
assets.description: Normalize asset inventory events from any source (osquery, CrowdStrike, Tenable, Qualys, Intune, Jamf, ServiceNow) to the unified asset.* schema. Called by source-specific sub-pipelines after their own field extraction. DC-2 (2026-09-18): this pipeline no longer computes its own m_26_14.integrity_hash; every inventory stream composes m_26_14-log-integrity-settings, so the final chain's m_26_14-log-integrity-hash writes the one canonical event.hash over the stored document (and m_26_14.integrity_hash as a one-release copy).

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-triage-classify
assets.description: M-26-14 unknown-device TRIAGE classifier. Reads one canonical asset doc (m_26_14-assets) and routes previously-unknown/unmanaged entities into exactly one disposition with a recommended next step and an evidence trail. Enriches m_26_14-host-alert-lookup by host.name to fold in the COMPUTED rogue signal (correlated Security alerts), then runs a priority-ordered Painless classifier over {managed, alert_count, max_risk_score, asset.status, hardware.manufacturer, hardware.serial_number, first_seen, last_seen}. Stamps m_26_14.triage.{disposition, recommended_action, confidence, signals[], auto_actionable, alert_count, max_risk_score, classified_at} and state='proposed'. Intended as a _reindex dest pipeline from m_26_14-assets -> m_26_14-asset-triage (idempotent, _id=asset.id) so the canonical store is never clobbered. Dispositions: rogue->escalate_ir | decommissioned->retire | new_uninventoried->enroll | shadow_it->exception | needs_review->review | inventoried (managed, no action). auto_actionable flags the REVERSIBLE next steps (suppress/draft-enroll) that MAY be automated after policy sign-off; it never auto-executes here — all enforcement is human-gated by the m_26_14-unknown-device-triage workflow.

assets.name: m_26_14-estate-hook
assets.description: M-26-14 estate binding (D-03/D-04/D-07/D-13/D-17/D-18): runs the pack's final chain (m_26_14-final: event.ingested stamp, ingest lag, schema observables, asset context, zero-trust context, policy enforcement point, SHA-256 integrity hash) on streams whose index.final_pipeline slot the pack cannot take. Fleet integration templates compose .fleet_agent_id_verification-1 last, which fixes final_pipeline to .fleet_final_pipeline-1, so Fleet streams reach m_26_14-final only through the default-pipeline hooks (logs@custom for every logs-* stream, logs-<dataset>@custom for one dataset). The loader's opt-in estate stage installs a pipeline processor that calls this hook into those hook pipelines, merging with whatever the agency already has there. Idempotent: skipped when the document already carries m_26_14.ingest_lag_ms (a pack stream that also binds m_26_14-final as final_pipeline, or a document that passed a hook twice). Never fails ingestion: every stage of m_26_14-final carries its own failure handling (derivation stages degrade with tag m_26_14-final-degraded, the PEP fails closed to sharing_class restricted with tag m_26_14-pep-failed), and this processor's on_failure catches anything that still escapes, tagging m_26_14-estate-hook-failed. It deliberately does NOT set ignore_failure: Elasticsearch skips a processor's on_failure handlers when ignore_failure is true (verified on 9.5), which is why the first version of this hook could never record a failure (review finding R-43). STABLE NAME REQUIRED: referenced by name from agency-owned logs@custom pipelines, so this pipeline is bootstrap-installed, never version-prefixed. See docs/estate-binding.md.

assets.name: m_26_14-field-fidelity-pipeline
assets.description: M-26-14 A-3 dest pipeline (D-02/16): classifies the dataset's LRA category, converts the transform's presence counts to percentages against that category's contract, and computes the fidelity score (60% common fields, 40% category fields). Contract lists mirror field_contracts in m_26_14-config.

assets.name: m_26_14-final
assets.description: M-26-14 final pipeline: ingest-lag measurement (LRA 3.5 timeliness) + schema observables + asset context + zero-trust context + policy enforcement, chaining SHA-256 integrity hashing. Derivation stages degrade with a tag; the PEP stage fails closed to sharing_class restricted.

assets.name: m_26_14-geoip-location
assets.description: M-26-14: geo_point location for network flow src/dst (location-only merge; preserves existing country fields).

assets.name: m_26_14-hash-coverage-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for the m_26_14-hash-coverage-rollup transform (hourly hash-coverage ratio per dataset). Design call DC-4 (2026-09-18): every transform output carries the D-13 provenance append and derived stamp (producer, method, pack version, computation time) so consumer-without-producer and unstamped-derived-data classes are closed for this store. No field logic here; the transform body owns the aggregation.

assets.name: m_26_14-host-alert-summary-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for the m_26_14-host-alert-summary transform (rogue signal per host from Security alerts). Design call DC-4 (2026-09-18): every transform output carries the D-13 provenance append and derived stamp (producer, method, pack version, computation time) so consumer-without-producer and unstamped-derived-data classes are closed for this store. No field logic here; the transform body owns the aggregation.

assets.name: m_26_14-ingest-latency-pipeline
assets.description: Classify ingest-latency rollups per LRA category, attach thresholds, mark breaches (LRA 3.5 timeliness measure).

assets.name: m_26_14-inventory-csv
assets.description: Parses CDM/CMDB CSV export lines into the m_26_14-inventory contract and derives host.name so the 9.4 Entity Store mints canonical 'expected' host entities (decision #21). Expected column order: asset_id,hostname,component,type,criticality,source,last_seen,ip(optional). Header lines, comments (#), and blank lines are dropped; rows without an asset_id are dropped. WHAT THE STORE USES (validated on-cluster): host.name (lowercased asset.hostname) is the host-engine identity field -- the only load-bearing field for extraction besides @timestamp; the store recomputes entity.id='host:<host.name>' (ignores any entity.id we set) and RETAINS asset.id + asset.criticality on the entity (that retained asset.id is the canonical/inventory link the scoring collector joins on). Do NOT stamp event.dataset here: entity.source on the stored entity is the OBSERVED data_stream.dataset axis, and a value would make every inventory host look 'observed' and erase the coverage-gap signal. (We deliberately set no entity.* fields -- the 9.4 host engine ignores them.) Sets _id from asset.id so re-ingesting a refreshed export upserts rather than duplicates. JSON documents posted directly (already shaped) pass through apart from _id/@timestamp/host.name stamping. Set as index.default_pipeline on m_26_14-inventory* by the index template.

assets.name: m_26_14-log-integrity-hash
assets.description: M-26-14 Appendix C Element 5 Level 3 — log integrity hashing. Computes the SHA-256 fingerprint of canonical ECS event fields at ingest time into event.hash, the pack's ONE hash field (design call DC-2). Bound as the last stage of m_26_14-final (the m_26_14-log-integrity-settings component template applies it as final_pipeline), so the hash covers the stored, post-redaction document. m_26_14.integrity_hash is written as a copy for one release only.

assets.name: m_26_14-netobserved-reroute
assets.description: Map + reroute stock network-integration events into the M-26-14 network-observed device inventory (opt-in; attach via logs-<dataset>@custom).

assets.name: m_26_14-network-device-normalize
assets.description: Normalize passively-observed OT/IoT network device signals into the M-26-14 asset model (OUI vendor enrich, OT-protocol tagging, asset/host entity population).

assets.name: m_26_14-ntp-status-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for the m_26_14-ntp-status transform (latest NTP sample per host). Design call DC-4 (2026-09-18): every transform output carries the D-13 provenance append and derived stamp (producer, method, pack version, computation time) so consumer-without-producer and unstamped-derived-data classes are closed for this store. No field logic here; the transform body owns the aggregation.

assets.name: m_26_14-observed-freshness
assets.description: Stamps write-time @timestamp on entity documents. Shared dest.pipeline for BOTH the m_26_14-observed-assets transform (ledger) and the m_26_14-store-feed transform (discovery feed). Semantics: @timestamp = when this entity doc was last written; last_log = the entity's last source activity. Required because the entity store v2 extract task only looks back a short window (lookbackPeriod, default 24h) over @timestamp -- entity docs carrying old activity timestamps (back-filled data, transform resets) would otherwise be permanently invisible to entity extraction. Chicken-and-egg, round three.

assets.name: m_26_14-ops-metrics-derive
assets.description: M-26-14 D-19 ops-metrics derivation: hot/frozen split, bytes per document and estimated monthly cost per tier from the agency's rates, computed once per snapshot.

assets.name: m_26_14-osquery-normalize
assets.description: Normalize M-26-14 osquery asset inventory results — hardware, software, and network queries DC-2 (2026-09-18): this pipeline no longer computes its own m_26_14.integrity_hash; every inventory stream composes m_26_14-log-integrity-settings, so the final chain's m_26_14-log-integrity-hash writes the one canonical event.hash over the stored document (and m_26_14.integrity_hash as a one-release copy).

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-exceptions
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07 PEP stage 0, design call DC-1 (2026-09-18): managed-exception check. Looks up every type:exception row for the document's dataset (enrich policy m_26_14-pep-exception-lookup, up to 8 rows) and sorts them by expiry against ingest time. Rules whose exception is still in force are recorded in m_26_14.policy.exception_rules_active (evidence only: the stages themselves are not switched, the register documents a suppression the agency applies elsewhere). Rules whose exception has EXPIRED are recorded in m_26_14.policy.exception_rules_expired, the document is marked m_26_14.policy.exception_expired true and tagged m_26_14-pep-exception-expired, and m_26_14-pep-route then routes it to the restricted class: an expired exception is a policy bypass with no approval behind it, and the LRA's own anti-pattern is a bypass that persists silently. The document is kept (never dropped) so the evidence and the daily m_26_14-pep-expired-exception alert both survive. Stable name: called from m_26_14-policy-enforcement, so bootstrap-classified like the rest of the chain.

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-minimize
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07 PEP stage 2: per-dataset field minimization driven by the m_26_14-pep-policy store (enrich lookup; no policy row = no-op). An active managed exception naming pep-minimize for the dataset switches the stage off (DC-16; recorded in m_26_14.policy.exception_applied).

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-production-none
assets.description: M-26-14 D-11 production profile 'none' - no redaction. Provenance stamp and profile marker only, so even an unredacted production copy documents how it was made. Use only when the requesting authority is cleared for raw data (see docs/runbooks/authorized-production.md).

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-production-standard
assets.description: M-26-14 D-11 production profile 'standard' - re-applies the D-07 secret/identifier redaction bank (SSN, PAN, cloud keys, JWT, bearer, private keys, URL secrets) to the production copy and strips internal working fields. NOTE the redact processor is skip_if_unlicensed - below the Enterprise license floor it silently no-ops; the authorized-production workflow samples the output for residual patterns and the runbook requires manual review on basic-licensed clusters (COMPAT.md).

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-production-strict
assets.description: M-26-14 D-11 production profile 'strict' - the standard redaction bank plus removal of the raw payload (event.original) and direct personal identifiers. Reference shape; agencies extend the removal list to their own sharing agreement. Same skip_if_unlicensed caveat as the standard profile (COMPAT.md).

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-redact
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07 PEP stage 1: redaction. Pattern bank over normalized text fields and event.original. skip_if_unlicensed true: below the Enterprise design floor this stage silently no-ops (documented in COMPAT.md). An active managed exception naming pep-redact for the dataset switches the stage off (DC-16; recorded in m_26_14.policy.exception_applied).

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-route
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07 PEP stage 4: routing DECISION. Sets the restricted-routing marker only: a reroute processor cannot run under a final pipeline, so physical rerouting to the -restricted namespace is an @custom-pipeline wiring documented in docs/policy-enforcement.md, and access segregation is enforced by DLS on m_26_14.policy.sharing_class regardless of physical location. Since DC-1 (2026-09-18) the decision also fires on m_26_14.policy.exception_expired, set by the m_26_14-pep-exceptions stage, and moves such documents to the restricted sharing class.

assets.name: m_26_14-pep-tag
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07 PEP stage 3: policy tagging. Sensitivity and sharing class from the pep-policy row with documented defaults; HVA from Entity-Store asset criticality already enriched upstream.

assets.name: m_26_14-policy-enforcement
assets.description: M-26-14 D-07: the policy enforcement point (LRA 4.6). One controlled place, invoked from m_26_14-final BEFORE the integrity hash so the hash covers the stored, post-redaction document. Order: exceptions (DC-1 managed-exception check), redact, minimize, tag, route-decision. Every stage appends to m_26_14.provenance.transformations (D-13). Stable name: referenced by name from m_26_14-final, so bootstrap-classified like it.

assets.name: m_26_14-retention-horizon
assets.description: Dest pipeline for m_26_14-dataset-retention transform. Computes the empirical searchable horizon (horizon_days = ingest_time - min(@timestamp)) for each data_stream.dataset and sets the dataset field for enrich matching. Replaces ILM/tier/snapshot introspection with a measured quantity: how far back can we actually search? The snapshot/retrievable axis is dropped (decision #22); both s_days and r_days are set to horizon_days in downstream ladder math.

assets.name: m_26_14-retention-to-scores
assets.description: Dest pipeline for m_26_14-score-dataset-retention transform. Projects a m_26_14-retention doc into a m_26_14-scores dataset_retention doc. Enriches config thresholds and runs the retention_level ladder (same logic as score.py retention_level() with single-axis empirical horizon: s_days == r_days == horizon_days). Deterministic _id = 'dataset::<dataset>' so each run upserts in place.

assets.name: m_26_14-retirement-ledger
assets.description: Retirement ledger stamps: @timestamp, updated_at and event.ingested from the ingest clock when absent (R-70), D-13 provenance.

assets.name: m_26_14-score-entity-pipeline
assets.description: Dest pipeline for m_26_14-score-entity transform (Stage 1). Receives one entity-store doc per canonical or discovered host entity and scores it for inventory freshness and coverage. Enriches: (1) m_26_14-inventory by host.name -> asset.* (canonical marker: enrich succeeds IFF the entity maps back to an inventory row by hostname); (2) m_26_14-observed by host.name -> last_log, first_log, datasets, skew_exceeded; (3) m_26_14-config-enrich -> thresholds. Produces a combined element:'asset' doc per entity with score_inventory (0/1), score_coverage (0/1), effective_horizon_days, is_canonical, provenance, and quadrant. Deterministic _id = 'asset::<effective_asset_id>'. Phase 1 NOTE: spine IP-fold (folding observed-<ip>@collector entries into canonical entities via host.ip) is deferred to Phase 2 -- only exact host.name enrich matching is performed. Entities only discoverable via IP-keyed observed entries will appear as expected_silent until Phase 2. D-20: enriches the host's latest NTP sample (m_26_14-ntp-enrich) into evidence.ntp_attestation {synced, offset_ms, server, last_sample, threshold_ms, source}; synced is null (source none) when the System ntp data stream has no sample for the host.

assets.name: m_26_14-score-rollup-pipeline
assets.description: Dest pipeline shared by m_26_14-score-rollup (per-component) and m_26_14-score-rollup-enterprise transforms (Stage 2). Receives a pivot aggregation doc with fields: n (entity count), reporting (sum score_inventory), covered (sum score_coverage), min_horizon (min effective_horizon_days), and either asset.component (component rollup) or run_id='engine' (enterprise rollup). Enriches config thresholds, runs level_from_pct for inventory/coverage and retention_level for retention (same math as score.py with single-axis empirical horizon), and emits a combined element:'rollup' doc. Deterministic _id = 'rollup::<component|_enterprise>' so each run upserts.

assets.name: m_26_14-software-enrich
assets.description: Enrich M-26-14 software inventory records with the authorized-software catalog (Element 2 / SWAM) regardless of collection source

assets.name: m_26_14-software-latest-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for the m_26_14-software-latest transform (latest software state per host, package and category). Design call DC-4 (2026-09-18): every transform output carries the D-13 provenance append and derived stamp (producer, method, pack version, computation time) so consumer-without-producer and unstamped-derived-data classes are closed for this store. No field logic here; the transform body owns the aggregation.

assets.name: m_26_14-store-feed-provenance
assets.description: Dest pipeline for m_26_14-store-feed transform. Stamps write-time @timestamp for Entity Store lookback and promotes transform attestation aggregates into ECS fields the host engine uses for entity.source (data_stream.dataset) and operator triage (event.module, m_26_14.collector). Attestation means logs referenced this identity — not hardware proof.

assets.name: m_26_14-store-ingested
assets.description: Default pipeline for the pack stores that are written by API (loader seed, workflows, operators) rather than by a transform: m_26_14-config, m_26_14-pep-policy, m_26_14-validation-ledger. Stamps event.ingested at write time so the detection rules that read these stores can clock on `timestamp_override: event.ingested` (TRADE check 4) instead of reporting a partial failure on every run and falling back to @timestamp. Finding R-84 (first pubsec install, 2026-09-18). override:false keeps a backfilled event.ingested, matching m_26_14-final.

assets.name: m_26_14-timestamp-skew
assets.description: M-26-14 Appendix B.3 timestamp accuracy check (D-20). Compares the event @timestamp against its ingest reference (event.ingested when the document carries one, otherwise this pipeline's _ingest.timestamp); when absolute skew meets or exceeds thresholds.skew_seconds from the m_26_14-config default document (300 s if the config lookup misses), persists m_26_14.skew_seconds, m_26_14.skew_threshold_seconds and m_26_14.skew_exceeded:true. Below threshold nothing is stored (storage-frugal by design). Never fails ingestion. Chained as the skew stage of m_26_14-final, so every pack stream and every estate stream bound through m_26_14-estate-hook is covered without per-stream wiring; call it from a logs@custom pipeline only for streams outside the final chain.

assets.name: m_26_14-zone-enrich
assets.description: D-26 segmentation context (LRA App D.3.4). Resolves m_26_14.zt.segment from the agency zone table (m_26_14-zone-map range enrich over m_26_14-config zone_map rows) on the source address. Enrich-dependent; called from m_26_14-zt-context with ignore_missing_pipeline so a bare pipelines-only install stays valid.

assets.name: m_26_14-zt-context
assets.description: M-26-14 D-17: zero-trust decision context (LRA 6.2 / 5.5 / App C.4.2). Derives m_26_14.zt.* where ECS has no home - MFA result, device compliance, policy and segmentation decisions, east-west direction - from well-known source fields, additive only (override false everywhere). Chained from m_26_14-final; also attachable via any integration @custom pipeline for sources outside the pack streams. Starter per-source mappings: Okta, Entra ID, Intune, Jamf, zone-aware firewalls; the mapping table and extension guidance live in docs/zt-decision-context.md.

assets.name: m_26_14-ai-audit
assets.description: M-26-14 D-06 AI audit trail - copies every Agent Builder trace span into the m_26_14-ai-audit store (LRA 5.5)

assets.name: m_26_14-alert-coverage-daily
assets.description: M-26-14 Appendix B alert coverage — daily buckets per detection category

assets.name: m_26_14-alert-coverage-latest
assets.description: M-26-14 Appendix B alert coverage — latest alert per rule for readiness status

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-baseline-snapshot
assets.description: Daily snapshot of each asset's canonical state (OS version, software hash, network interfaces, encryption). Output to m_26_14-asset-baselines. Diff between current state and baseline drives detection rules 1-7.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-entity-resolution
assets.description: Resolve and merge asset inventory events from all sources into canonical asset records. Runs every 30 minutes. Groups by asset.id (deterministic UUID from serial/agent/MAC/hostname). Produces one upserted document per physical or virtual device.

assets.name: m_26_14-dataset-retention
assets.description: Stage 0 — empirical dataset retention (decision #22). Pivots over all log indices grouped by data_stream.dataset; computes first_log (min @timestamp = earliest log = empirical searchable horizon start) and last_log (max @timestamp). Writes one doc per dataset to m_26_14-retention; the m_26_14-retention-horizon dest pipeline computes horizon_days = (ingest_time - first_log) / 86400000. This replaces ILM/tier/snapshot introspection: we measure realized retention rather than policy promises. After data changes, re-execute the m_26_14-observed-enrich policy so Stage 1 picks up fresh horizons. Frequency: 1h (same source pattern as m_26_14-observed-assets). Run BEFORE m_26_14-score-dataset-retention and m_26_14-score-entity.

assets.name: m_26_14-field-fidelity
assets.description: M-26-14 A-3 (decisions D-02/16): hourly per-dataset presence counts for the LRA 6.3 common fields and App D category-fidelity signals; the dest pipeline classifies the LRA category, computes percentages against that category's contract, and scores fidelity. Read beside the native Data Set Quality _ignored rate: this measures field-absent, native measures present-but-unmappable.

assets.name: m_26_14-hash-coverage-rollup
assets.description: Hourly hash-coverage rollup per data stream: total docs, integrity-hashed docs, and hash_ratio (hashed/total). Feeds the m_26_14-ml-element5-hash-coverage ML job with a TRUE coverage ratio - zero-coverage buckets exist as hash_ratio=0 documents instead of being invisible (the pre-redesign datafeed filtered to hashed docs only, so a dataset whose hashing stopped simply vanished from the feed).

assets.name: m_26_14-host-alert-summary
assets.description: Computes the ROGUE signal for unknown-device triage. Pivots the Security detection alerts (.alerts-security.alerts-*) by host.name into one summary doc per host: alert_count, max_risk_score, max_severity, last_alert, and the set of firing rule names. The m_26_14-asset-triage-classify pipeline enriches against this summary (via the m_26_14-host-alert-lookup enrich policy) so an unmanaged asset with correlated high-severity alerts is routed 'rogue' from REAL detections rather than a seeded flag. host.name MUST be keyword on the dest index (see m_26_14-asset-triage index template) for the enrich match to work.

assets.name: m_26_14-ingest-latency
assets.description: D-03 ingest timeliness (LRA 3.5): continuous hourly rollup of m_26_14.ingest_lag_ms (stamped by the m_26_14-final pipeline) per data_stream.dataset into m_26_14-ingest-latency. Emits p50/p95/max lag, doc count, and skew count (negative-lag docs, excluded from percentiles). The m_26_14-ingest-latency-pipeline dest pipeline classifies each bucket into a coarse LRA category, attaches the category threshold, and marks breaches for the ES|QL rule and collection-coverage panels.

assets.name: m_26_14-ntp-status
assets.description: Latest NTP sample per host from the System integration ntp data stream (metrics-system.ntp-*, Stack 9.2+): system.ntp.offset (estimated offset of the local clock relative to the server, nanoseconds) and system.ntp.host (the server compared against). One document per host.name in m_26_14-ntp-status, read by the m_26_14-ntp-enrich policy so the entity scoring pipeline can write evidence.ntp_attestation on every asset score (LRA 6.3, memo Appendix B timestamp accuracy). Bootstrap-only: the source is an integration data stream the agency enables, not a pack stream. Runs unattended so a cluster where the ntp data stream is not yet enabled keeps the transform alive (source pattern matches nothing) until samples arrive.

assets.name: m_26_14-observed-assets
assets.description: Entity discovery for known AND unknown assets, regardless of ingest pathway (decisions #17/#18). A runtime field performs multi-entity EXTRACTION per document -- existence attestation, not single attribution -- emitting every entity the document proves exists; the terms group_by fans each document into every matching entity bucket. Slots: SELF (host.name, host.hostname, agent.name, deduplicated), OBSERVER (observer.hostname else observed-<observer.ip>), DEVICE (log.syslog.hostname else observed-<log.source.address ip, port stripped> -- only collector-stamped fields, so ordinary network events never mint entities from conversation participants), and an empty-document fallback (observed-<host.ip or source.ip>) reachable only when no slot yielded anything. A collector-mediated syslog document therefore attests the collector, any observer, and the downstream device -- up to three entities from one document. Output docs carry host.name + @timestamp, eligible as an entity-store feed: add m_26_14-observed to the Security default data view.

assets.name: m_26_14-score-dataset-retention
assets.description: Stage 0b — promotes m_26_14-retention docs to dataset_retention score docs in m_26_14-scores. Uses a latest transform (unique_key: dataset) so each dataset has exactly one current score doc. The m_26_14-retention-to-scores dest pipeline enriches config thresholds, runs the retention_level ladder, and sets element:'dataset_retention', asset.id:'dataset:<ds>', _id:'dataset::<ds>'. These docs are the in-stack equivalent of score.py's per-dataset dataset_retention docs. Run AFTER m_26_14-dataset-retention (source must have data). Frequency: 1h offset +5m from Stage 0.

assets.name: m_26_14-score-entity
assets.description: Stage 1 — per-entity inventory + coverage scoring (decisions #21/#22). Sources from the Entity Store v2 backing alias 'entities-latest-default' (one doc per canonical host entity). Uses a latest transform (unique_key: entity.id) to pass each entity doc through the m_26_14-score-entity-pipeline dest pipeline, which: (1) enriches m_26_14-inventory by host.name to establish canonical status (asset.id present = inventory-sourced); (2) enriches m_26_14-observed by host.name for last_log/first_log/datasets; (3) enriches config thresholds; (4) computes score_inventory (0/1 freshness within 7d), score_coverage (0/1 has datasets), effective_horizon_days (empirical retention from first_log), provenance, is_canonical, and quadrant. Produces element:'asset' docs in m_26_14-scores with _id='asset::<effective_asset_id>'. Space: default (hardcoded; make a Fleet policy var at M8). Phase 1 NOTE: IP-fold (folding observed-<ip>@collector into canonical entities) is deferred -- entities only visible via IP-keyed observed entries appear as expected_silent. See m_26_14-score-entity-pipeline _meta for details. Run AFTER enrich policies are executed and m_26_14-observed has data.

assets.name: m_26_14-score-rollup
assets.description: Stage 2 — per-component rollup. Reads canonical entity score docs from m_26_14-scores (element:asset, is_canonical:true, written in the last 2h), groups by asset.component, and aggregates n (entity count), reporting (sum score_inventory), covered (sum score_coverage), min_horizon (min effective_horizon_days). The m_26_14-score-rollup-pipeline dest pipeline enriches config thresholds, runs level_from_pct for inventory/coverage and retention_level for retention, and emits a combined element:'rollup' doc per component with score_inventory/score_coverage/score_retention (0-4 each). _id = 'rollup::<component>'. The 2h @timestamp range filter prevents stale entity docs from inflating the denominator (H3: entity-left-store staleness). Run AFTER m_26_14-score-entity completes its cycle.

assets.name: m_26_14-score-rollup-enterprise
assets.description: Stage 2b — enterprise rollup. Same source and logic as m_26_14-score-rollup but groups by run_id (always 'engine' for in-stack docs) to produce a single enterprise-wide doc. The m_26_14-score-rollup-pipeline dest pipeline detects the absence of asset.component (enterprise case) and sets asset.id:'_rollup' with no component, _id='rollup::_enterprise'. score_inventory/score_coverage/score_retention (0-4) represent the enterprise-wide maturity levels across ALL canonical entities in all components. There is no waterline doc (out of scope for Phase 1 — operations and log_mgmt are deferred to separate efforts). Run AFTER m_26_14-score-entity completes its cycle; same offset as m_26_14-score-rollup.

assets.name: m_26_14-software-latest
assets.description: Latest-state software inventory per host + package + category, from the canonical enriched stream. Powers the m_26_14-asset-security-software-removed rule: a security package whose package_last_seen goes stale while the host's asset.last_seen stays fresh has left the snapshot. Category is a group key (stable per package) so dest docs carry it as a flat dotted field without top_metrics Map-wrapping. Dest docs are only rewritten when new source docs arrive for the bucket, so a removed package's dest doc freezes - rules reading this index need a lookback covering the staleness horizon (R7 uses now-30d).

assets.name: m_26_14-store-feed
assets.description: Entity-store FEED (decisions #20/#21): emits ONLY entities the store cannot discover from raw documents -- syslog-header-named devices, observers, and hostname-less devices (device/observer/fallback slots; never the self slot). IP-keyed entities use observed-<ip>@<collector>; collector suffix prefers observer.name (stable ingest pool/site id) over host.name so load-balanced Logstash backends do not duplicate the same device. The dest pipeline (m_26_14-observed-freshness, shared with the ledger) stamps write-time @timestamp so the store's lookback window can see fresh feed docs. These land as host entities keyed by host.name (real syslog hostname or observed-<ip>@<collector>); they carry NO asset.id, which is exactly how operators distinguish them from canonical inventory entities (observed-but-unexpected until resolved via entity.relationships.resolution.resolved_to to a canonical host:<host.name> entity). Add THIS index (m_26_14-store-feed), not m_26_14-observed, to the Security default data view; feeding the full ledger would duplicate every Agent host. The ledger remains the universal measurement index.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-baseline-lookup
assets.description: Serves the certified configuration baseline hash per asset (m_26_14.baseline_hash from m_26_14-asset-baselines, matched on asset.id) to the m_26_14-asset-drift pipeline, which compares it with the current snapshot hash and sets m_26_14.drift_detected on the canonical asset record. Re-executed hourly by the m_26_14-enrich-refresh workflow.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-liveness
assets.description: Serves asset.last_seen, asset.criticality and asset.managed from the canonical asset index (m_26_14-assets, matched on host.name) to the m_26_14-asset-context stage of the final pipeline, which is how every log document picks up its HVA criticality and managed state at ingest (decision D-18). Re-executed hourly by the m_26_14-enrich-refresh workflow.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-readiness-lookup
assets.description: Serves the whole asset.* and m_26_14.* block of the canonical asset record (m_26_14-assets, matched on host.name) to m_26_14-asset-entity-store-enrich, which attaches asset type, criticality, data classification and readiness posture to Security alerts and log events for investigation and Entity Store context.

assets.name: m_26_14-authorized-software
assets.description: SWAM allowlist lookup: serves the authorized-software catalog row (m_26_14-authorized-software-catalog, matched on package.name) to the m_26_14-software-enrich and m_26_14-osquery-normalize pipelines, which mark each installed package authorized, denied or uncataloged with its category, publisher, end-of-life flag and CDM approval provenance. The catalog ships as a starter seed (m_26_14-authorized-software-seed.ndjson); re-execute the policy after editing it.

assets.name: m_26_14-config-enrich
assets.description: Serves the single configuration document (m_26_14-config, matched on config_key) to the scoring dest pipelines so every score carries the thresholds and attestations in force when it was computed: Appendix C per-element level ladders, the retention floors and the NTP attestation switch. Editing m_26_14-config and re-executing this policy is how an agency tunes the pack without touching a pipeline.

assets.name: m_26_14-host-alert-lookup
assets.description: Serves the computed rogue signal per host (alert_count, max_risk_score, last_alert, severities and the firing rule names from m_26_14-host-alert-summary, matched on host.name) to the m_26_14-asset-triage-classify pipeline, so an unmanaged device with correlated high-severity Security alerts is routed to the rogue disposition from real detections rather than a seeded flag. Execute after the m_26_14-host-alert-summary transform has populated its index.

assets.name: m_26_14-hold-no-delete
assets.description: M-26-14 hold policy for PLAIN indices (not data streams): authorized-production copies (m_26_14-production-*, decision D-11) and legal-hold retained copies (m_26_14-retained-*). Hot (0-90d) searchable, frozen via searchable snapshot (90d+) retrievable, NO delete phase and NO rollover: a plain index has no rollover alias, so the m_26_14-logs-l3-no-delete policy (which rolls over at 1d) parks such an index in ILM ERROR at its first rollover check. assets.name: m_26_14-logs-hva-extended

assets.name: m_26_14-gate1-approval-advance
assets.description: Gate 1 approval handler: hourly check for indices whose LATEST ledger record is approved_gate1. Writes a pending_gate2 record (time-suffixed id, R-71) and opens the Gate 2 Kibana Case. IMPORTANT: no ILM change happens at Gate 1; the index stays on its no-delete policy until Gate 2 approval, when m_26_14-gate2-execute-deletion switches it to the delete-enabled variant. Deployment tokens are substituted by load_bootstrap.py (watchers stage) from its targets and M_26_14_WATCHER_AUTH; without the auth header the loader registers this watch inactive (R-67).

assets.name: m_26_14-gate1-detect-frozen-aged
assets.description: Gate 1 detection: daily scan for m_26_14 indices in the frozen ILM phase whose lifecycle age (from rollover, ILM lifecycle_date_millis) has reached the retirement floor for its ILM policy, with no open retirement request. Design call DC-14: the floor comes from the m_26_14-config default row (retirement.floor_days.<policy>, 'never' excludes the policy: HVA-extended, hold-no-delete), falling back to floor_days.default and then to metadata retention_days when the row or key is absent; each ledger record carries the floor it was judged against. Writes one pending_gate1 ledger record per candidate (time-suffixed id, R-71) and opens one Kibana Case. Deployment tokens __ES_HOST__ / __KIBANA_HOST__ / __AUTH_HEADER__ are substituted by bootstrap/m_26_14/load_bootstrap.py (watchers stage) from its own targets and M_26_14_WATCHER_AUTH; without the auth header the loader registers this watch inactive (R-67). Frozen backing indices are named partial-.ds-<stream>-<gen> by ILM; the ledger records that name. An index covered by an active legal hold (newest record legal_hold_initiated, source_index names its data stream or matches its backing-index name, ILM mount prefix ignored) is not proposed; the Gate 2 guard applies the same test. A cancelled index is re-proposed only after recheck_after_days. The Kibana Workflow m_26_14-data-retirement-gate1-detect is the same detection on the Workflows control plane (design call DC-15).

assets.name: m_26_14-gate2-execute-deletion
assets.description: Gate 2 execution: hourly check for indices whose LATEST ledger record is approved_gate2. This is the ONLY step that makes deletion possible: it switches the index from its no-delete ILM policy to the delete-enabled variant, then ILM takes a compliance snapshot (wait_for_snapshot) before deleting. Safety guards: (1) index name must contain m_26_14 (scope guard against forged records), (2) any active legal hold whose source_index names the candidate's data stream or matches its backing-index name blocks retirement; the candidate is compared with its ILM mount prefix (partial- frozen, restored- other phases) stripped, since ILM renames a mounted searchable snapshot and a hold written against .ds-<stream>-* would otherwise never match (R-68), (3) a missing delete_policy on the request chain causes a skip, never a default. Deployment tokens are substituted by load_bootstrap.py (watchers stage); without M_26_14_WATCHER_AUTH the loader registers this watch inactive (R-67).

assets.name: m_26_14-jit-audit
assets.description: JIT access daily auditor (Element 5 L4): runs daily at 13:00 UTC, inventories all status=active grants in m_26_14-jit-grants, and appends a daily report document to m_26_14-jit-audit-reports flagging any grant active longer than 72 hours. Long-running grants violate the just-in-time principle — review and revoke or re-justify them. Pair with a detection rule or connector on the report index for ISSO notification. Deploy via scripts/deploy.py which substitutes __ES_HOST__/__KIBANA_HOST__/__AUTH_HEADER__ tokens.

assets.name: m_26_14-jit-expiry
assets.description: JIT access auto-revoker (Element 5 L4): every 15 minutes, finds m_26_14-jit-grants documents with status=active whose expires_at has passed, deletes the backing role mapping (m_26_14-jit-{grant_id}) — which revokes the role instantly across all realms — and writes a status=expired audit record. Grants are role mappings, not user edits, so revocation is a single idempotent DELETE and never touches passwords. Deploy via scripts/deploy.py which substitutes __ES_HOST__/__KIBANA_HOST__/__AUTH_HEADER__ tokens.

assets.name: m_26_14-selective-copy-legal-hold
assets.description: Legal hold / selective copy template. MUST be registered INACTIVE (PUT _watcher/watch/<id>?active=false; the loader does this) because the reindex runs in the input phase: an active scheduled fire would reindex the placeholder params. Trigger by hand with POST _watcher/watch/m_26_14-selective-copy-legal-hold/_execute after setting metadata.params (source_index may be a data stream name, which reindexes every backing index including frozen mounts, or an index pattern). Reindexes the source into a named retained index, assigns m_26_14-hold-no-delete (no rollover, no delete; R-69), executes the readiness SLM policy, writes a legal_hold_initiated ledger record (time-suffixed id, R-71) whose source_index is what m_26_14-gate2-execute-deletion checks, and opens a Kibana Case. Release the hold by writing a cancelled record for the retained index. Deployment tokens are substituted by load_bootstrap.py (watchers stage) from its targets and M_26_14_WATCHER_AUTH (R-67).
