assets.name: M-26-14 AI: Security AI Assistant Knowledge Base or Product Documentation Modified
assets.description: LRA Section 5.5 (decision D-06, follow-up R-25): the Security AI Assistant grounds its answers in a knowledge base (agency entries plus Elastic product documentation). Changing that corpus changes what the assistant tells analysts without any prompt being visible, which is a manipulation path the LRA asks agencies to log. The Kibana audit log records knowledge_base_entry_create/update/delete and product_documentation_create/update/delete with the acting user. The Security AI Assistant has no trace stream; this rule and the connector-lifecycle rule are the only pack-side evidence for it, and neither captures conversation content.

assets.name: M-26-14 AI: Kibana Connector Created, Updated or Deleted
assets.description: LRA Sections 5.5 and 8.1 (decision D-06, follow-up R-25): a Kibana connector is the platform's binding to an external model provider, and every AI feature in Kibana (Agent Builder, Security AI Assistant, Attack Discovery, Automatic Import) calls its model through one. The Kibana audit log records connector_create, connector_update and connector_delete with the acting user and the connector's saved-object id; it does not record the connector TYPE, so this rule fires for every connector (email, Slack, LLM) and triage resolves the type from the connectors API. A new or changed LLM connector is a change to the model lineage of every AI-derived value the platform produces (LRA 4.4) and a configuration change to a high-value asset (8.1). No connector-execute or LLM-call audit event exists in Kibana; per-call evidence comes from the Agent Builder trace stream (m_26_14-ai-audit) and the token usage data stream, not from this rule.

assets.name: M-26-14 AI: Prompt-Injection Phrasings in Agent Builder Traces
assets.description: LRA Section 5.5 (decision D-06): matches a fixed list of prompt-injection and jailbreak phrasings (phrase matching only; it does not detect tool misuse, identity change or out-of-scope index access) inside the logging platform's own AI audit trail - the m_26_14-ai-audit store that the m_26_14-ai-audit transform copies from Agent Builder trace spans (Kibana 9.5+). The AI that answers auditors is itself a high-value asset; an attempt to steer it is a security event against the logging platform, not a UX curiosity. Matches only fire when the agencyBuilder tracing content settings are enabled, because the matched fields (gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.tool.call.arguments, gen_ai.system_instructions) are simply absent otherwise - an agency that keeps content capture off accepts that this rule is blind, and records that decision (see docs/ai-audit.md).

assets.name: M-26-14 AppA-L: New/Rogue Device on Network Segment (Passive)
assets.description: Detects a device (normalized host.name = netdev-<mac>) appearing for the first time on a network.segment in the passively-observed device inventory (logs-m_26_14_netobserved.devices-*). Uses a compound new_terms tuple (network.segment + host.name), so a brand-new MAC OR a known device that migrates to a new segment fires. This is the agentless complement to AppB-E (Fleet enrollment): it catches OT/IoT devices (PLCs, cameras, sensors) that never run an Elastic Agent and are invisible to agent-based HWAM. M-26-14 Appendix A requires a complete hardware inventory including devices that cannot host an agent. Correlate alerts with the osquery HWAM inventory; no match = unmanaged/unauthorized. Statistically backed by the m_26_14-ml-element1-new-network-device rare() job. Baseline the stream 7 days before enabling so each segment's normal device population is learned.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-A: Azure/Entra Failed Logins Followed by Success - Potential Brute Force
assets.description: Detects five or more Azure/Entra sign-in failures for the same user and source IP within the evaluation window, followed by at least one successful sign-in from that same pair. This pattern is consistent with password guessing / brute-force activity against Entra ID. Maps to M-26-14 Appendix B Category A identity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-A: Linux SSH Failed Logins Followed by Success - Potential Brute Force
assets.description: Detects ten or more SSH authentication failures for the same user, source IP, and host within the evaluation window, followed by at least one successful SSH login from that same tuple. This pattern is consistent with password guessing / brute-force activity against Linux servers. Maps to M-26-14 Appendix B Category A identity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-A: Okta Failed Logins Followed by Success - Potential Brute Force
assets.description: Detects five Okta authentication failures for the same user within 10 minutes, followed by a successful Okta authentication or session start. This pattern is consistent with password guessing / brute-force activity against the agency Okta tenant. Maps to M-26-14 Appendix B Category A identity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-A: Windows Failed Logins Followed by Success - Potential Brute Force
assets.description: Detects five or more Windows authentication failures (Event IDs 4625, 4771) for the same user within 10 minutes, followed by a successful logon (Event ID 4624). This pattern is consistent with password guessing / brute-force activity against Active Directory. Maps to M-26-14 Appendix B Category A identity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-B: Repeated Outbound Connections to Single External IP on Non-Standard Port
assets.description: Detects M-26-14 Appendix B §5(b) network activity: a single source host establishes 20 or more egress connections to the same external IP on a non-standard port within the evaluation window, with first-to-last connection spanning at least 25 minutes. Aggregates egress network events from Elastic Network Traffic data by source IP, destination IP, destination port, and host.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-C: Mass File Access by User and Process
assets.description: Detects M-26-14 Appendix B §5(c) object/resource access activity: a single user and process pair generates 500 or more file access, open, or read events within the evaluation window. Aggregates endpoint/audit file events by user, host, and process, and reports access count, distinct path count, and per-minute access rate.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-D: New Account Created Then Successfully Used
assets.description: Detects a sequence within 1 hour where a user account is created (IAM user-account added/created with user.target.name set) and that same account name then successfully authenticates via Windows Event ID 4624 or 4648. Aggregates by matching user.target.name to user.name across the two stages. Maps to M-26-14 Appendix B Category D privileged and account activity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-E: OT Device Configuration Change Outside Change Window (Dragos)
assets.description: Detects Dragos-reported OT device configuration changes, firmware updates, or parameter writes occurring outside the maintenance change window. The window is evaluated in UTC: before 06:00, at or after 18:00, or on Saturday/Sunday. Adjust the site_offset noted in the query and setup guide to shift the window to site-local time; ES|QL cannot evaluate a site-local calendar directly.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-E: New OT Asset by Serial Number (Dragos)
assets.description: Detects a Dragos-observed OT asset whose serial number (dragos.asset.serial_number) has not been seen in the last 7 days. Serial number is the asset identity key; events without a serial number are excluded. First-seen does not by itself establish an unauthorized device: alerts from this rule feed the M-26-14 unknown-device triage flow (classify, route, gated action) alongside the passive network-observation and Fleet enrollment first-seen signals.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-E: First-Seen Elastic Agent Enrollment
assets.description: Detects an Elastic Agent enrollment event whose agent.id has not been seen in the last 7 days, using Fleet enrollment telemetry (event.action: enroll). First-seen enrollment does not by itself establish a rogue or unauthorized device: alerts from this rule feed the M-26-14 unknown-device triage flow (classify, route, gated action) alongside the passive network-observation and Dragos first-seen signals.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-F: EDR Tamper Indicators After High-Severity Endpoint Alert
assets.description: Detects a sequence on one host where a high or critical severity Elastic Endpoint alert (event.severity >= 65) is followed within 10 minutes by an EDR tamper indicator: an EDR/AV process ending, a security service being stopped or disabled (Windows System events 7036/7040), or a process opening a handle to an EDR binary (Sysmon event 10). Each indicator is circumstantial on its own; the correlation with a preceding high-severity alert on the same host is the detection signal and warrants immediate triage.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-G: IoC — Malicious Domain in DNS Queries
assets.description: Matches DNS query names against threat intelligence domain indicators of compromise (IoCs) as required by M-26-14 §5(g). Fires when dns.question.name in DNS traffic matches a known-malicious domain in the agency's threat intelligence feed. Covers C2 domain callbacks, DGA (Domain Generation Algorithm) beaconing to known patterns, phishing infrastructure, and malware distribution domains. Complements the IP match rule for C2 traffic that leverages domain fronting or CDN infrastructure (where the IP may be shared/benign but the domain is malicious). Required by M-26-14 §5(g) for federal agencies to continuously monitor for domain-based IoCs from authoritative threat intelligence sources. INTERIM RULE: Elastic is adding a prebuilt Threat Intel Domain Indicator Match rule upstream; retire this custom rule when it ships. The other AppB-G indicator types (IP, file hash, URL, email, Windows registry) are covered by the existing prebuilt Threat Intel Indicator Match rules, which this pack enables instead of shipping custom copies.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-H: Off-Hours Bulk Process Execution
assets.description: Detects M-26-14 Appendix B §5(h) anomalous activity signal: a non-system user account starts 50 or more processes on a single host between 22:00 and 05:00 UTC within the evaluation window. Aggregates process start events by user and host. Blunt-threshold heuristic intended as a low-confidence anomaly signal / hunt cue, not a confirmed insider-threat or compromise detection: scheduled maintenance, patching, backups, CI runners, and global-timezone workforces all produce legitimate off-hours bulk execution.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-I: High Outbound Network Data Volume
assets.description: Detects egress network volume above a fixed threshold: more than 500 MB of outbound bytes from a source host (and process when present) to non-RFC1918 destinations within the evaluation window. Aggregates network events by source IP, host, and process. Fixed-threshold egress-volume monitoring signal with no baseline or destination-rarity context; treat alerts as a volume anomaly to investigate, not confirmed exfiltration.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-J: Inbound Connection Followed by Script/LOLBin Then Admin-Port Egress (2h)
assets.description: Detects a three-event sequence on the same host within 2 hours: an inbound network connection from a non-RFC1918 source IP, then a start of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, regsvr32.exe, rundll32.exe, or certutil.exe by a non-SYSTEM user, then an egress connection to destination ports 445, 135, 139, 3389, 22, 5985, or 5986.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-J: Inbound Connection Followed by Script/LOLBin Then Admin-Port Egress (4h)
assets.description: Detects the same three-event sequence as the 2h AppB-J rule, with a 4-hour maxspan. Complement to m_26_14-appendixb-j-apt-chain-2h.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-K: Appendix B Alert Activity by Category (Daily)
assets.description: Reports which M-26-14 Appendix B detection categories (A-J) produced Security alerts during the previous 24 hours, aggregated by category tag. This is an alert-activity report only: it does not verify rule enablement, rule execution health, or source-data ingestion freshness, and absence of a category here can mean either no qualifying activity or a broken rule.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-K: No Appendix B Alerts in 30 Days (Coverage Silence)
assets.description: Global coverage tripwire: fires when zero Security alerts carrying any Appendix B category tag (A-J) were produced in the last 30 days. Total pack silence over 30 days indicates disabled rules, broken ingestion, or missing data sources rather than a genuinely quiet environment. This rule performs a single global check; it does not identify which individual categories are silent.

assets.name: M-26-14 AppB-L: OT-Protocol Egress to Unexpected Destination
assets.description: Fires when an industrial control protocol (Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP, BACnet, PROFINET, OPC-UA) is observed toward a destination outside private, loopback, link-local, and CGNAT address space (IPv4 and IPv6) in the passively-observed device inventory (logs-m_26_14_netobserved.devices-*). A destination IP is required to match. Passive flow records in this stream carry no network.direction field, so classification is destination-based: any globally routable destination for an OT protocol is treated as egress. Normal OT traffic stays local (PLC <-> historian/SCADA on the same segment); an industrial protocol reaching a public IP is a high-signal indicator of compromise, exfiltration, or dangerous misconfiguration. Maps to M-26-14 Appendix B 5(b) network monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: Baseline Drift Detected
assets.description: Detects managed assets whose current inventory snapshot no longer matches their recorded baseline hash. The drift hash is a composite of OS identity, hardware serial, and encryption state, so any of those components changing raises this alert; the specific changed component is determined during triage by comparing the current snapshot against the baseline record, not by this rule.

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: Critical Asset Check-in Stopped
assets.description: Detects managed HVA-level assets (asset.criticality extreme_impact or high_impact, the Kibana asset-criticality vocabulary the pack uses for HVA tagging) whose inventory check-in (asset.last_seen) is more than 24 hours old. Reads the current-state m_26_14-assets population over a 30-day rule window so that assets which stopped updating remain visible to the rule (a stopped asset's record is, by definition, no longer refreshed; a short lookback would age it out of evaluation entirely).

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: Config Drift — Disk Encryption Disabled on Managed Asset
assets.description: Detects managed assets where disk encryption is recorded as false in the canonical asset index. Disk encryption is required for all managed endpoints under FISMA/FedRAMP controls and is a key M-26-14 Element 1 HWAM compliance indicator. A managed asset with encryption disabled may indicate a policy violation, a failed BitLocker/FileVault key protector, or an active attack (encryption stripped prior to data exfiltration). Fires whenever the canonical record shows asset.managed: true AND asset.compliance.encrypted: false, regardless of drift state.

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: New Local User Account Observed
assets.description: Detects a host + username combination never seen in the prior 7 days on the local user-inventory stream. The combination key is intentional: the same username appearing on a new host is a distinct local account. This rule claims only that a new local account appeared; it does not determine whether the account is privileged - administrator verification is a triage step (UID 0, or membership in Administrators/wheel/sudo groups from the group-inventory collection).

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: New Network Interface (First-Seen MAC)
assets.description: Detects a MAC address never seen in the prior 7 days on the asset-inventory stream. The osquery interface collection emits flat `host.mac` values; this rule keys first-seen detection on that single stable field. A new MAC on an existing host indicates an added or changed network interface (USB adapter, virtual interface, NIC swap) and feeds the unknown-device triage flow for classification.

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: Security Software Removed or Stopped Reporting
assets.description: Detects security-category software (EDR, AV, osquery, audit tooling; catalog categories 'security' and 'security-tooling') that has stopped appearing in inventory snapshots for more than 24 hours on a host that is itself still checking in. The host-alive guard (asset.last_seen within 24h via the inventory enrich lookup) separates package removal from whole-host offline, which the check-in-stopped rule covers. Reads the m_26_14-software-latest transform destination (latest state per host + package).

assets.name: M-26-14 Asset: Unauthorized or Uncataloged Software Installed
assets.description: Detects software on managed hosts that is not explicitly approved in the SWAM authorized-software catalog: packages the catalog marks denied (authorization_state: denied) and packages absent from the catalog entirely (authorization_state: unknown, stamped explicitly at enrich time so catalog misses cannot fail open). Grouped by host and package name so each alert identifies the offending package.

assets.name: M-26-14 OPS: Canary Detection Path Check
assets.description: LRA Section 4.7 and App E.12.1 (decision D-09): synthetic canary documents are injected every cycle by the m_26_14-canary-inject workflow, and this rule exists to exercise the detection-engine path end to end WITHOUT touching real rules: it matches only documents marked m_26_14.canary true. An alert from this rule is a PASS signal, consumed by the m_26_14-canary-verify workflow (stage 3, alerted); silence within a canary's SLA is the failure. Do not tune, silence, or add exceptions here: this rule firing on schedule is the evidence that alerting works.

assets.name: M-26-14 OPS: Canary Validation Stage Failed
assets.description: LRA Sections 3.5 and 4.7 (decision D-09): every canary cycle writes a three-stage verdict (arrived, parsed, alerted) to m_26_14-validation-ledger, and this rule fires when any cycle in the window records a failed stage. A failed 'arrived' means the ingest path for that source class is down or rerouting; 'parsed' means the pipeline chain degraded (check the failure store and the schema-drift job); 'alerted' means the detection path is broken even though data flows: the exact silent failure mode the LRA's validation measure exists to catch.

assets.name: M-26-14 DM: Data Retirement — Gate 1 Approval Pending
assets.description: Detects M-26-14 managed indices awaiting Gate 1 (pre-retirement) approval in the two-gate data retirement chain. Fires when the newest pending_gate1 record for an index is more than 24 hours old and no approved_gate1 or cancelled record for the same index is newer than it (latest-record semantics: the ledger is append-only, so a cancellation older than a fresh re-proposal no longer masks it). The 90-day lookback (on event.ingested, stamped by the ledger pipeline) covers the realistic pending horizon; a request pending longer than that is itself a process failure and should be caught by periodic manual audit of m_26_14-retirement-requests.

assets.name: M-26-14 DM: Data Retirement — Gate 2 Deletion Approval Pending
assets.description: Detects M-26-14 managed indices awaiting Gate 2 (deletion authorization) in the two-gate data retirement chain. Fires when the newest pending_gate2 record for an index is more than 24 hours old and no approved_gate2, scheduled_for_deletion, cancelled or deletion_completed record for the same index is newer than it (latest-record semantics over an append-only ledger). Gate 2 is the last human checkpoint before deletion; the compliance snapshot is taken after approval, when ILM advances to the delete phase behind wait_for_snapshot. The 90-day lookback (on event.ingested, stamped by the ledger pipeline) covers the realistic pending horizon.

assets.name: M-26-14 HVA: Configuration Change on High Value Asset
assets.description: Alerts on any configuration change event on an HVA-tagged asset, immediately. On general hosts, configuration changes feed the baseline-drift workflow; on HVAs every change is alert-worthy on its own (decision D-18, LRA Section 5.5 / App D.9).

assets.name: M-26-14 HVA: Failed Authentication Burst on High Value Asset
assets.description: Detects 3 or more failed authentication events against a single user on an HVA-tagged asset within the rule window. The general-population brute-force rules tolerate longer runs; HVA assets alert at threshold 3 (decision D-18, LRA Section 5.5 / App D.9: HVA logging and detection must be materially stronger than general enterprise logging).

assets.name: M-26-14 HVA: New Process Executable on High Value Asset
assets.description: Fires when a process executable never seen on an HVA-tagged asset in the last 7 days starts there. General enterprise hosts get behavioral ML; HVA assets alert on first sight (decision D-18, LRA Section 5.5 / App D.9).

assets.name: M-26-14 HVA: Raw-Retention Lock Removed From Config
assets.description: Alerts daily while the raw_retention.hva entry in the m_26_14-config default document is anything but keep_locked (missing counts). Decision D-12 forbids raw-payload (event.original) retention opt-out for HVA-tagged data and D-18 locks the row; until this rule, the lock was a seed value plus prose, and an edit to drop was accepted everywhere (review finding R-39). Posture rule: it reads configuration, not telemetry.

assets.name: M-26-14 OPS: Ingest Latency Category Threshold Breach
assets.description: LRA Section 3.5 timeliness measure (decision D-03): fires when a dataset's p95 ingest lag (measured by the m_26_14-final pipeline, rolled up hourly by the m_26_14-ingest-latency transform) exceeds its LRA-category threshold in two or more hourly buckets within the three-hour rule window. Thresholds ship as agency-tunable defaults in m_26_14-config (mirrored in the m_26_14-ingest-latency-pipeline). Sustained breach means logs are arriving too late for the timeliness the category demands: check the collector or forwarder queue (Logstash PQ/DLQ, decision D-05), polled-source cadence, and pipeline backpressure before assuming a source outage. Negative-lag (clock skew) documents are excluded from percentiles and owned by the m_26_14-timestamp-skew asset.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-A/D — Anomalous Authentication Failure Count for User (Entity Store)
assets.description: Detects users experiencing an anomalously high count of authentication failures compared to their individual historical baseline. This rule references the Elastic Security prebuilt ML job `m_26_14_auth_high_count_logon_fails_ea`, which must be installed and running in Kibana ML before this detection rule can be activated. Unlike static threshold rules (e.g., >10 failures in 5 minutes), this ML rule detects failure counts that are anomalous relative to each user's own baseline — catching slow brute-force attacks, password spraying against specific accounts, and targeted credential stuffing that would evade fixed-threshold rules. Satisfies M-26-14 Appendix B Category A (identity anomalies) and Category D (privilege escalation precursor — repeated failures before a successful login). MITRE ATT&CK: T1110 Brute Force (TA0006 Credential Access) including subtechniques T1110.001 Password Guessing, T1110.002 Password Cracking, T1110.003 Password Spraying, and T1110.004 Credential Stuffing.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-A — Rare Source IP for Authenticating User (Entity Store)
assets.description: Detects authentication events originating from source IP addresses that are statistically rare for a specific user, based on that user's historical authentication pattern. This rule references the Elastic Security prebuilt ML job `m_26_14_auth_rare_source_ip_for_a_user_ea`, which must be installed and running in Kibana ML before this detection rule can be activated. An authentication from a rare source IP may indicate: account compromise with attacker authenticating from an unfamiliar location, credential theft and replay from a different network segment, authorized VPN/travel scenario (generates false positives but should be documented), or insider threat actor using an unusual workstation. Satisfies M-26-14 Appendix B Category A (identity and authentication anomaly detection) at L4 maturity. MITRE ATT&CK: T1078 Valid Accounts (TA0001 Initial Access, TA0003 Persistence, TA0004 Privilege Escalation, TA0005 Defense Evasion).

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-A/H — Suspicious Login Activity (Entity Store)
assets.description: Detects anomalously high volumes of authentication activity for a user, scored against that user's own historical baseline by the Elastic Security anomaly job m_26_14_suspicious_login_activity_ea (security_auth module job m_26_14_suspicious_login_activity_ea, installed with the m_26_14_ prefix). High-volume login anomalies support M-26-14 Appendix B Category A (identity) and Category H (anomalous activity) monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-B/G — DNS DGA/High-Entropy Query Anomaly
assets.description: Detects clients (source.ip) generating DNS queries with statistically higher entropy than their individual historical baseline — a primary behavioral indicator of DGA (Domain Generation Algorithm) based command-and-control malware. Unlike static threat intelligence rules (Category G IoC matching), this ML rule detects previously-unseen DGA families by identifying the one statistical signal this job actually models: anomalously high character entropy in dns.question.name relative to that client's own baseline (high_info_content). TLD distribution, query cadence, and per-application profiling are NOT modeled — pair with Category G IoC matching and network session analytics for those angles. Satisfies M-26-14 Appendix B Category B (C2 beaconing/covert channel detection) and supports Category G (threat intelligence enrichment) when DGA domains are submitted to threat intelligence sharing. Requires Zeek DNS logging (logs-zeek.dns*) or Packetbeat DNS (logs-network_traffic.dns*). The datafeed applies Zeek trailing-dot normalization via script_fields to ensure consistent domain entropy calculation across DNS data sources.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-B — Network Traffic to Rare Country Anomaly
assets.description: Detects network connections to countries that are statistically rare for a specific host or user's historical network communication pattern. This rule references the Elastic Security prebuilt ML job `m_26_14_rare_destination_country`, which must be installed and running in Kibana ML before this detection rule can be activated. Traffic to a rare country may indicate: data exfiltration over the C2 channel to adversary infrastructure hosted abroad, beaconing to command-and-control servers using legitimate cloud providers in unusual geographic regions, misuse of a VPN or proxy to obscure true destination, or supply-chain compromise via update server redirection. The ML approach complements static geo-blocking rules by detecting rare (but not blocked) country connections that deviate from the per-host baseline. Satisfies M-26-14 Appendix B Category B (C2 and covert channel detection) at L4 maturity. MITRE ATT&CK: T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel (TA0011 Command and Control) and T1071 Application Layer Protocol.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-H — Monitored Host Went Silent (Entity Store)
assets.description: Entity Store security_host _ea low_count job: a monitored host's event volume collapsed to near-zero, an Appendix B Anomalous-Activity signal (agent tampering, outage, or exfil-staging cleanup).

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-H — Rare Process Execution on Linux Host
assets.description: Detects rare or anomalous process execution on Linux hosts by comparing observed processes against each host's historical execution baseline. Binds the OS-scoped Elastic Security anomaly job m_26_14_v3_rare_process_by_host_linux_ea (security_linux_v3 module, installed with the m_26_14_ prefix), so Linux anomalies alert only through this rule. Supports M-26-14 Appendix B Category H anomalous-activity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: AppB-H — Rare Process Execution on Windows Endpoint
assets.description: Detects rare or anomalous process execution on Windows endpoints by comparing observed processes against each host's historical execution baseline. Binds the OS-scoped Elastic Security anomaly job m_26_14_v3_rare_process_by_host_windows_ea (security_windows_v3 module, installed with the m_26_14_ prefix), so Windows anomalies alert only through this rule. Supports M-26-14 Appendix B Category H anomalous-activity monitoring.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: Element 1 — Asset Coverage Drop Anomaly
assets.description: Detects anomalous drops in the number of distinct assets reporting to each M-26-14 inventory source. The ML job models low_distinct_count(host.name) partitioned by m_26_14.coverage_source (osquery, intune, network_discovery, or dataset fallback) over the controlled inventory observation streams — so the signal is “how many unique assets checked in”, not raw document volume. When a source’s distinct-asset count drops anomalously vs. its rolling baseline (target: ≥20% of previously-reporting assets silent), this rule fires to indicate a potential compliance posture failure under M-26-14 Element 1 (Comprehensive Asset Coverage): network connectivity issues, EDR/agent tampering, unauthorized host decommissioning, or adversarial network isolation. Element 1 requires ≥80% daily asset coverage at L2 and ≥95% at L3; the coverage PERCENTAGE itself is computed by the coverage transform and dashboard — this rule is the anomaly tripwire for sudden drops.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: Element 2 — Log Ingestion Rate Drop Anomaly
assets.description: Detects anomalous drops in the per-dataset log ingestion rate, measured on ARRIVAL time: the ML job clocks on event.ingested (stamped by the Fleet final pipeline on managed streams and by the M-26-14 normalize pipelines on custom streams), so late backfills cannot mask a real pipeline outage and delayed batches do not read as silence. Unlike Element 1 (which tracks distinct assets), this rule monitors whether the data streams themselves are receiving events at the expected rate. An ingestion rate drop can indicate pipeline failures (Logstash, Elastic Agent integration, ingest processor), data source misconfigurations, or adversarial log suppression. Scope limitation: the model only covers datasets that have reported at least once — a dataset that has NEVER arrived cannot form a partition; never-onboarded sources are surfaced by the Appendix B-K coverage rule and the coverage dashboard. M-26-14 Element 2 requires specific log types to be ingested at appropriate fidelity; a sustained ingestion drop risks compliance gaps in the audit log record and may impair threat detection coverage across Appendix B categories.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: Element 3 — Rule Category Alert Silence Anomaly
assets.description: Detects when a specific M-26-14 Appendix B rule category has produced statistically fewer security alerts than expected based on its historical baseline. This rule complements the ES|QL-based m_26_14-appendixb-k-coverage-gap rule: where the ES|QL rule fires on absolute zero alerts, this ML rule detects anomalously low (but non-zero) alert volume — a subtler and often more dangerous signal. A rule category going quiet may indicate: (1) the underlying detection rule was accidentally disabled, (2) the data source feeding that category has been silenced or tampered with, (3) an adversary has learned to operate below the detection threshold, or (4) a genuine reduction in relevant activity. The ML model accounts for weekly seasonality and long-term trend, distinguishing a truly anomalous silence from an expected quiet weekend. Partitions by m_26_14.category, derived at DATAFEED time from the rule’s Appendix-B-<letter> tag via runtime mapping — no ingest-pipeline dependency on .alerts-security.*. Meta and self-referential rules (readiness-health wrappers, the meta degradation rule, Appendix B-K coverage-gap alerts) are excluded from the feed to avoid contaminating the silence model with its own health signals. Scope limitation: a category whose rules have never alerted cannot form a partition; day-zero absence is owned by the Appendix B-K rule and the coverage dashboard.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: Element 4/5 — Anomalous ILM/Retention State Change
assets.description: Detects anomalous index administrative operations in Elasticsearch audit logs — deletions, settings updates, forcemerge, and close operations that affect retention. Two detectors on the ECS field elasticsearch.audit.action: (1) high_count per action fires on volume spikes vs. the learned baseline (bulk purge patterns); (2) rare action per user.name fires when an account performs an index-admin action that is rare FOR THAT ACCOUNT — targeted retirement abuse that evades volume thresholds. elasticsearch.audit.indices rides as an influencer, so every anomaly names the affected index. While scheduled ILM operations are normal, anomalous spikes may indicate unauthorized data deletion, retention tampering, or adversarial destruction of audit evidence. Supports Element 4 (Minimum Retention Periods) and Element 5 (Log Integrity and Chain of Custody). REQUIRES success-level audit events (access_granted): a failure-only audit configuration produces zero documents for this job’s datafeed. The higher anomaly threshold (85) is intentional: ILM operations are inherently bursty, and a high threshold reduces false positives from large-scale but authorized ILM runs.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: Element 5 — Log Hash Coverage Drop Anomaly
assets.description: Detects an anomalous drop in the integrity-hash coverage RATIO for one or more M-26-14 log data streams. The m_26_14-hash-coverage-rollup continuous transform computes, per dataset per hour, total docs vs. integrity-hashed docs (event.integrity.hashed:true) and the resulting hash_ratio; the ML job models low_mean(hash_ratio) per dataset over that rollup index. This is a true coverage measurement: a dataset whose hashing silently stops produces hash_ratio=0 rows the model can alarm on, where the previous hashed-docs-only design simply went blind. M-26-14 Element 5 requires cryptographic integrity verification of agency log data via the m_26_14-log-integrity-hash ingest pipeline; a ratio drop means that pipeline is failing, bypassed, or an unhashed source was introduced into a hashed stream — undermining the chain-of-custody and tamper-evidence requirements of Element 5. Scope limitation: a dataset that has NEVER been hashed carries a baseline ratio of 0 and will not anomaly; never-onboarded streams are surfaced by the hash-coverage dashboard. MITRE relevance: T1565.001 (Stored Data Manipulation) and T1070 (Indicator Removal).

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: Meta Readiness Degradation — Any Element Anomaly
assets.description: Meta readiness degradation rule — fires when ANY of the 7 readiness-health M-26-14 ML jobs produces an anomaly above threshold. Serves as a single alert entry point for ISSO compliance health monitoring. Individual element rules (m_26_14-ml-e1-* through m_26_14-ml-e5-* and m_26_14-ml-schema-drift) provide specific context; this rule is the catch-all when ISSO wants a single alert stream for compliance posture degradation. Reference the individual element rules for specific investigation guidance. Jobs monitored: m_26_14-ml-element1-asset-coverage (Element 1 asset count), m_26_14-ml-element2-ingestion-rate (Element 2 data stream ingestion), m_26_14-ml-element3-rule-silence (Element 3 detection rule category silence), m_26_14-ml-element4-ilm-anomaly (Element 4/5 retention/ILM operations), m_26_14-ml-element5-hash-coverage (Element 5 log integrity hash ratio), m_26_14-ml-element1-new-network-device (Element 1 new/rogue device on a network segment), and m_26_14-ml-schema-drift (Element 2 parser failure and schema drift). The DNS entropy job (m_26_14-ml-catb-dns-entropy) is a threat-detection job with its own wrapper rule (m_26_14-ml-catb-dns-dga) and is not part of this readiness roll-up. This meta rule simplifies ISSO daily compliance review: a single alert queue, one rule to check each morning, with links to element-specific rules for drill-down.

assets.name: M-26-14 ML: D-04 Schema Drift per Data Stream
assets.description: Detects schema drift on pack data streams using the m_26_14-ml-schema-drift anomaly detection job. The m_26_14-final pipeline stamps every document with m_26_14.schema.top_level_keys (the sorted top-level field names) and m_26_14.schema.field_count. Detector 0 (rare top-level key, partitioned per data_stream.dataset) fires when a field family APPEARS on an established dataset: a source upgrade, a parser change, a misrouted stream. Detector 1 (mean field_count per dataset) fires when fields DISAPPEAR, the context-discarding normalization the CISA Logging Reference Architecture section 8.3 avoid-list names, or when the document balloons. Hard mapping conflicts belong to the daily field-caps workflow and outright parse failures to the failure-store rule; this rule covers the silent middle: documents that still index but no longer look like they did. The job clocks on event.ingested (arrival time) so backfills do not smear drift windows.

assets.name: M-26-14 Time Sync: Host NTP Offset Exceeded
assets.description: Alerts when a host's most recent System integration ntp sample reports a clock offset beyond 1000 ms against its configured NTP server (decision D-20, LRA 6.3, memo Appendix B timestamp accuracy). system.ntp.offset is the estimated offset of the local clock relative to the server in nanoseconds; the rule converts to milliseconds. The 1000 ms threshold mirrors thresholds.ntp_offset_ms in the m_26_14-config default document (an ES|QL rule cannot read the config document, so the value is mirrored here on purpose; change both together). Per-host attestation evidence lives on the asset score document (evidence.ntp_attestation) from the same samples via the m_26_14-ntp-status transform and m_26_14-ntp-enrich policy.

assets.name: M-26-14 Posture: Ops Metrics Snapshot Stale
assets.description: Alerts daily when the newest m_26_14-ops-metrics-* snapshot is older than 48 hours or no snapshot exists at all. The D-19 cost-value view renders stored daily snapshots from the m_26_14-ops-metrics-snapshot workflow (ships disabled); without this rule a workflow that was never enabled, lost its schedule, or started failing left the dashboard showing yesterday's numbers indefinitely with nothing to say so (review finding R-47). Posture rule: it reads the pack's own evidence store, not telemetry.

assets.name: M-26-14 OPS: PEP Exception Expired But Still Present
assets.description: LRA Section 8.3 names unmanaged exceptions as an anti-pattern; the pack's answer (decision D-07) is a managed-exceptions register in m_26_14-pep-policy: every suppression of a policy enforcement rule carries a dataset, the rule suppressed, a reason, an approver, and an expiry. This rule fires when an exception's expiry has passed while the row is still present: the exception is no longer managed. Either renew it (new approver and expiry) or delete the row and let the PEP rule apply again.

assets.name: M-26-14 OPS: Ingest Pipeline Failures Detected (Failure Store)
assets.description: LRA Sections 4.7 and 7.3, Appendix E.5.3/E.6.4 (decision D-04): parse failures and mapping conflicts are captured in each pack data stream's failure store instead of bouncing to the client, and this rule fires when a stream accumulates 10 or more failed documents in a 15-minute window, grouped by target index, error type, failing pipeline, and processor tag (every pack processor is tagged <pipeline>:<step>:<type>, enforced by the build lint). Failure documents hold the ORIGINAL, pre-pipeline source: they may contain data the pipelines normally redact, so read_failure_store is granted only to roles cleared for raw data (decision D-07 policy item).

assets.name: m_26_14 security alerts
assets.description: Security detection alerts (.alerts-security.alerts-default). The view behind the alert-coverage and HVA detection-density panels and the AppB-K coverage rules.

assets.name: m_26_14 field fidelity
assets.description: Hourly field-fidelity scores per dataset (m_26_14-field-fidelity, time field bucket_start) written by the m_26_14-field-fidelity transform. Backs the Field Fidelity dashboard and the HVA-versus-general fidelity comparison.

assets.name: m_26_14 inventory
assets.description: Canonical asset inventory (m_26_14-assets*), one document per resolved device. Backs the HWAM, SWAM, gaps, lifecycle and drift dashboards.

assets.name: m_26_14 ingest latency
assets.description: Hourly ingest-lag rollups per dataset (m_26_14-ingest-latency, time field bucket_start) from the m_26_14-ingest-latency transform. Backs the timeliness panels on Collection Coverage and HVA Differentiation.

assets.name: m_26_14 logs
assets.description: All log data streams (logs-*). The general Discover view for the log estate, used by the drill-down links on the coverage dashboards.

assets.name: m_26_14 observed hosts
assets.description: The entity observation ledger (m_26_14-observed): every host, observer and device the log estate proves exists, with first and last activity. No time field: it is a current-state index, one document per entity.

assets.name: m_26_14 ops metrics
assets.description: Daily ops-metrics snapshots (m_26_14-ops-metrics*) written by the m_26_14-ops-metrics-snapshot workflow. Backs the Cost and Operational Value dashboard.

assets.name: m_26_14 scores
assets.description: Readiness score documents (m_26_14-scores*): per-entity, per-dataset and per-component rollups written by the scoring transforms. Backs the Maturity Overview, Collection Coverage and Preflight dashboards.

assets.name: m_26_14 store feed
assets.description: The Entity Store discovery feed (m_26_14-store-feed*): syslog-named and IP-keyed devices the store cannot mint from raw documents. Add it to the Security default data view so those devices become host entities.

assets.name: m_26_14-inventory
assets.description: OMB M-26-14 HWAM/SWAM/network endpoint inventory — feeds m_26_14-osquery-normalize.

assets.name: M-26-14 After-Action Report Agent
assets.description: Generates audit-ready After-Action Reports (AARs) for closed incidents. Reconstructs the incident timeline from Elastic logs and Cases, identifies affected assets and data classifications, analyzes the detection path, and drafts the AAR in M-26-14/FISMA format.

assets.name: M-26-14 POA&M Drafting Agent
assets.description: Queries Elastic for open M-26-14 readiness findings (unresolved Cases, retirement gaps, unclassified data, recurring alerts) and drafts properly formatted Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) entries per FISMA requirements.

assets.name: M-26-14 Threat Investigation Agent
assets.description: Autonomously investigates M-26-14 security alerts by querying logs, entity risk scores, asset inventory, attack discoveries, and related cases. Produces a structured, audit-ready investigation summary for the Kibana Case.

assets.name: m_26_14-asset-inventory-search
assets.description: Searches the M-26-14 unified asset canonical index for hardware and software assets. Returns asset criticality, data classification, ownership, M-26-14 element mapping, and readiness posture. Use this tool to look up an asset by hostname, IP, or software name during threat investigation or POA&M drafting.

assets.name: m_26_14-classification-audit-query
assets.description: Queries the M-26-14 data classification audit index (m_26_14-data-classification-requests) using ES|QL. Use to find data streams awaiting a sensitivity determination (state = classification_pending) or to review completed classifications. Each classification_pending record is a potential POA&M item under Appendix A incidental sensitive-data exposure / Log Management.

assets.name: m_26_14-readiness-posture-query
assets.description: Queries M-26-14 alert-coverage posture (Collection Operations) from m_26_14-metrics-alert-coverage using ES|QL. Returns, per Appendix B logging category, whether detections are active/covered plus recent rule and alert counts. Use for POA&M drafting to surface categories with no or partial detection coverage. For classification gaps use m_26_14-classification-audit-query; for retirement gaps use m_26_14-retirement-audit-query.

assets.name: m_26_14-retirement-audit-query
assets.description: Queries the M-26-14 data retirement ledger (m_26_14-retirement-requests) using ES|QL. Use this tool to find indices pending retirement, legal hold status, gate approval states, and the audit trail for deletion decisions; useful for POA&M drafting to surface open retirement gaps. IMPORTANT latest-record semantics: the ledger is append-only. Every state change (detection, approval, cancellation, execution, legal hold, release) is a NEW record with its own request_id, so a pending_* record is current only if no newer record exists for the same index_name. Before reporting an index as pending or held, sort its records by @timestamp descending and read the newest state. A cancelled record for a retained index (state legal_hold_initiated earlier) means the hold is released.

assets.name: M-26-14 ATT&CK Coverage Snapshot
assets.description: Monthly coverage snapshot (decision D-15): counts the pack's tagged detection rules and how many are enabled, records disabled-rule names, and writes the result to m_26_14-validation-ledger as trendable evidence for LRA Sections 3.1/9.1.

assets.name: M-26-14 Authorized Production
assets.description: Manual workflow for authorized external log production (decision D-11, LRA Section 7.4): role-gated, opens a Case with the request SLA, copies the scoped set through a named redaction profile into a no-delete production index, verifies counts and redaction, snapshots the result, and writes a full transformation manifest to m_26_14-production-ledger.

assets.name: M-26-14 Canary Inject
assets.description: Injects one marked synthetic document per source class through the normal default pipeline every 15 minutes (decision D-09). The companion verify workflow checks arrived/parsed/alerted per canary and writes verdicts to m_26_14-validation-ledger.

assets.name: M-26-14 Canary Verify
assets.description: Hourly three-stage verification (arrived, parsed, alerted) of the synthetic canaries injected by m_26_14-canary-inject; writes one aggregate verdict document per source class to m_26_14-validation-ledger (decision D-09).

assets.name: M-26-14 Data Classification Intake
assets.description: Manual workflow for initiating data classification review of a newly discovered index or data stream. Opens a Kibana Case assigned to the data steward with classification guidance, records classification_pending state in the audit index, and sends a notification. Satisfies M-26-14 sensitive-data classification requirements before access controls are applied.

assets.name: M-26-14 Data Retirement — Gate 1 Approval Handler
assets.description: Manual workflow: run after Gate 1 has been approved for a specific index. Records approved_gate1 and pending_gate2 states in the audit index and opens a Gate 2 (final deletion authorization) Kibana Case. No ILM change happens at Gate 1 — the index keeps its no-delete policy until the Gate 2 Execution workflow switches it to the deletion-enabled variant, after which ILM wait_for_snapshot enforces a durable snapshot before deletion.

assets.name: M-26-14 Data Retirement — Gate 1 Detection
assets.description: Scheduled daily scan (and manual trigger) that uses Elastic AI Agent to identify M-26-14 frozen indices whose lifecycle age has reached the retirement floor for their ILM policy (m_26_14-config retirement.floor_days, fallback 365 days) with no open retirement request. Creates a Gate 1 approval Kibana Case and a detection-run audit record. Part of the M-26-14 two-gate data retirement workflow.

assets.name: M-26-14 Data Retirement — Gate 2 Execution
assets.description: Manual workflow: run after Gate 2 final deletion authorization is confirmed for a specific index. Switches the index from its no-delete ILM policy to the deletion-enabled variant — the only step that makes deletion possible. ILM wait_for_snapshot then enforces a durable compliance snapshot before the delete action executes. Records the scheduled_for_deletion audit state.

assets.name: M-26-14 Enrich Refresh
assets.description: Hourly re-execute of the seven enrich policies whose source index is written by transforms or ingest (assets, observed, baselines, host-alert summary), so enrich-backed pipelines such as the D-18 HVA feeder serve current data instead of the install-time snapshot.

assets.name: M-26-14 Legal Hold — Selective Copy
assets.description: Manual workflow for legal hold or regulatory data preservation. Reindexes a source index into a named retained index with no-delete ILM policy, triggers readiness snapshot, and opens a Kibana legal hold Case with full audit trail. Satisfies M-26-14 forensic preservation requirements before the retirement lifecycle begins.

assets.name: M-26-14 Mapping Conflict Check
assets.description: Daily schema-health check: calls _field_caps across the pack data streams, finds any field mapped as more than one type across backing indices, and writes a run summary with the conflicted fields to m_26_14-pipeline-health for the pipeline-health view and the D-04 evidence trail.

assets.name: M-26-14 Ops Metrics Snapshot
assets.description: Daily operational-metrics snapshot (decision D-19): store size and doc counts for the logging estate with a frozen-tier split and the agency's unit costs, written to the month's m_26_14-ops-metrics-YYYY-MM index whose default pipeline derives hot bytes, bytes per document and estimated monthly cost per tier for the cost-value view (LRA Section 9.3).

assets.name: M-26-14 Retrieval Drill
assets.description: Monthly retrieval demonstration (decision D-10): timed ES|QL query set with tier attribution, snapshot restore with count and integrity-hash coverage verification, evidence to m_26_14-validation-ledger, Case on failure.

assets.name: M-26-14 Unknown-Device Triage
assets.description: Manual workflow that routes a classified unknown/unmanaged device to a disposition-specific Kibana Case (rogue / decommissioned / new_uninventoried / shadow_it / needs_review) with the recommended next step and evidence, records routing state in the m_26_14-asset-triage ledger, and notifies the responder. All enforcement is human-gated. Satisfies M-26-14 Element 1 (detect + action unauthorized/unknown assets).
